newsitem.title: CHINA: China marks anniversary of Japan invasion.
newsitem.headline: China marks anniversary of Japan invasion.

text.p: Chinese academics met on Friday to mark the 60th anniversary of the Marco Polo Bridge incident that sparked the full-scale Japanese invasion of China, the official Xinhua news agency said.
A clash between Chinese and Japanese troops at the bridge in southwestern Beijing on July 7, 1937, escalated into a war that raged across China for almost a decade.

Beijing has been eager to publicise events marking its war of resistance against Japanese agression as a way to boost patriotic sentiment among its huge population and to remind Tokyo of its imperial past.

Japan's eventual defeat in 1945 was a major event in China's return to national pride, as was the July 1 return of the British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, Xinhua quoted academics at the memorial meeting as saying.

"Victory over Japan, as well as Hong Kong's return to the motherland are... milestones of the struggle of the Chinese people to wipe out century-old humiliation," it quoted one Chinese scholar as saying.

Ever-sensitive relations between Beijing and Tokyo have been tested over the last year by rows over a disputed island group in the East China Sea and by Japan's planned revision of its security alliance with the United States.
